language.description: The language of the words the statusline writes (labels, units of waiting such as `ago`, the names of effort levels): en, zh-Hans for Chinese in simplified characters, and zh-Hant for traditional; zh and zh-TW are read as zh-Hans and zh-Hant, and any other tag is refused. Durations, token counts, the dollar sign and clock times are written the same in every language, and a clock time follows the system locale and the clock settings.

preset.description: A named bundle of settings (layout.header, layout.rows, git.enabled, git.showDirty, git.showAheadBehind, git.showLineDiff, jj.enabled, jj.showDirty, jj.showConflicts, usage.resetLabel and context.breakdown) that this layer sets beneath the keys it names itself and above everything the shallower layers set: standard is the statusline's own default, everything claude-hud's default configuration draws plus agent-shim's own segments; full, essential and minimal are claude-hud's presets. Each draws the model, project and version control segments, the extra segment once extra.command is set, and the context row; standard adds the provider, route, account, identity and headroom segments and the quota and added directories rows, with the reset label and the token breakdown from its threshold, full adds the effort, advisor, version, output style, cost, session name and duration segments and the quota, added directories, memory, environment, tools, skills, mcp, agents, todos, prompt cache, compactions and session tokens rows, with the token breakdown from its threshold, essential adds the duration, the added directories row and the tools, agents and todos rows, and minimal adds the added directories row alone.

header.description: The header segments to draw, in drawing order; a segment left out is hidden, and an empty list hides the header.

rows.description: The rows to draw below the header, in drawing order; a row left out is hidden, and an empty list hides every row.

mode.description: How the statusline is laid out: expanded draws the header and then the rows, each on lines of its own as layout.merge allows, and compact draws the header segments and every row's content on one line, starting a new line only where the line would be wider than the width. layout.mergeBars, layout.merge, layout.rightAlign and layout.rule have no effect in compact.

rule.description: Whether a rule is drawn across the line between the header and the rows beneath it, as wide as the header's widest line (at least 20 columns, at most the width); it is drawn only when both the header and the rows have something to show, and not in the compact layout.

mergeBars.description: Whether bar rows that sit next to each other in layout.rows share a line, and one grid, when they fit (the context and quota bars do by default); when false each bar row is on a line of its own, its bars aligned to its neighbours' while the line is wide enough for that. A row of text is never joined by this setting, whichever form the quota row takes: layout.merge does that.

merge.description: Groups of rows that share a line when they sit next to each other in layout.rows and fit on one line together, and are drawn on lines of their own when they do not; each group names at least two rows, and no row belongs to two groups. A group may mix bar rows and rows of text, which are joined with the separator when every member is a single line. Bar rows outside a group follow layout.mergeBars. A group in which no row has anything to show draws nothing: one with a row of text in it still ends a run of bars sharing a line, as an empty row of text does, and one of bar rows alone is left out, so the bars either side of it share as if it were not there.

rightAlign.description: Rows that start the right-aligned part of a merged line: the first of them to appear on a line, and the rows after it, are pushed to the right edge, with the gap padded by spaces. A row named here must belong to a group in layout.merge, and it has no effect when it is the first row of its line.

maxWidth.description: The exact width in columns lines are drawn to when the client reports none and the COLUMNS environment variable names none, in place of the default width it would assume for the terminal; unlike a terminal's width, it is not reduced by the columns Claude Code keeps back for itself. It is 0, to leave it unset, or from 20 to 1000; a value outside that is refused, not clamped.

forceMaxWidth.description: Whether maxWidth is the exact width lines are drawn to for whatever the client reports, even when the terminal is narrower or wider; it needs maxWidth to be set.

format.description: How the model's name is written: full is the name as the client gives it, compact drops a context-window suffix such as (1M context), and short also drops a leading Claude.

override.description: A name to show in place of the client's own model name, whatever model is running; empty shows the model's own name. A dynamic mode's served model still follows it.

source.description: Where the model's name comes from: client is the name the client reports (its display name, else its model id, each trimmed and read as absent when blank), transcript is the model the session's last reply came from (what a proxy actually served), and auto uses the transcript's model only when it is not a Claude model, which is what a proxy redirect looks like.

platform.description: Whether the model segment ends with the label claude-hud draws beside the model name, chosen from the client's environment and model id as claude-hud chooses it, the first that holds: Bedrock when CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK is 1, Vertex when CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX is 1, MiniMax when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (else ANTHROPIC_API_BASE_URL), trimmed, is https://api.minimax.io/anthropic or https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic compared by origin and path with any trailing slash, query or default port ignored, and Enterprise when the model id is opusplan, sonnetplan or haikuplan in any case. Nothing is drawn when none holds, and the label stands alone when no name is known: the client's display name and model id are both absent or blank, no override is set, and model.source supplies no transcript name (under transcript it supplies one when the transcript has an assistant record with a model, and under auto only for such a model that is not a Claude one), or model.format leaves nothing of the name. The switches and the model ids are Claude Code's, so an Antigravity client never draws the label. It is not the provider segment, which names the agent-shim provider the launch selected and the door routes to.

name.description: A label to show in place of the launch's provider name, or on its own when the launch has no provider; empty shows the provider's own name.

parts.description: What the account segment says about the login account, in drawing order: the account's email address, its organisation (shown for team and enterprise accounts) and its plan. A part left out is hidden, and an empty list hides the segment.

userLength.description: The most characters of the account's email address to show, with an ellipsis after a cut one; 0 shows all of it.

format.description: How the reasoning effort is written: full is a symbol and the level (a filled circle that grows with the level, then the name), symbol is the symbol alone, and text is the level's name alone. A level with no symbol is always written as its name.

override.description: A name to show for the advisor model in place of the one the session's transcript records; empty shows the transcript's, prettified.

bar.description: Whether the context row draws its bar, or only its figures on one line of text.

value.description: The context figure: both (the tokens held against the window, then the percentage), percent, tokens, or remaining (the percentage of the window left).

warnAt.description: The whole percentage of the context window at which the context bar turns yellow when bar.gradient is off (a bar.gradient of use holds the warning colour exactly where the bar turns yellow, half a point below this percentage for the rounding, and width colours a bar by its cells, not its use, once a cell of its used part is drawn; both fall back to the band colours when a stop's colour is default or dim, and width also when no cell of its used part is drawn); it must be below context.criticalAt. The percentage is rounded to a whole number before it is compared with this, as claude-hud rounds it, so a reading within half a point below counts as at it. It is the context bar's own threshold, apart from bands.warnAt, which colours the other bars and the context row's cache hit share, and its default is claude-hud's contextWarningThreshold. A layer may write null to return it to its default when a shallower layer sets it.

anyOf.description: The whole percentage of the context window at which the context bar turns yellow when bar.gradient is off (a bar.gradient of use holds the warning colour exactly where the bar turns yellow, half a point below this percentage for the rounding, and width colours a bar by its cells, not its use, once a cell of its used part is drawn; both fall back to the band colours when a stop's colour is default or dim, and width also when no cell of its used part is drawn); it must be below context.criticalAt. The percentage is rounded to a whole number before it is compared with this, as claude-hud rounds it, so a reading within half a point below counts as at it. It is the context bar's own threshold, apart from bands.warnAt, which colours the other bars and the context row's cache hit share, and its default is claude-hud's contextWarningThreshold.

criticalAt.description: The whole percentage of the context window at which the context bar turns red when bar.gradient is off (a bar.gradient of use holds the critical colour from where the bar turns red, half a point below this percentage for the rounding, and width colours a bar by its cells, not its use, once a cell of its used part is drawn; both fall back to the band colours when a stop's colour is default or dim, and width also when no cell of its used part is drawn), and from which the token breakdown appears while context.breakdownAt is unset. The percentage is rounded to a whole number before it is compared with this, as claude-hud rounds it, so a reading within half a point below counts as at it. It is the context bar's own threshold, apart from bands.criticalAt, which colours the other bars and the context row's cache hit share, and its default is claude-hud's contextCriticalThreshold, which also starts claude-hud's breakdown. A layer may write null to return it to its default when a shallower layer sets it.

anyOf.description: The whole percentage of the context window at which the context bar turns red when bar.gradient is off (a bar.gradient of use holds the critical colour from where the bar turns red, half a point below this percentage for the rounding, and width colours a bar by its cells, not its use, once a cell of its used part is drawn; both fall back to the band colours when a stop's colour is default or dim, and width also when no cell of its used part is drawn), and from which the token breakdown appears while context.breakdownAt is unset. The percentage is rounded to a whole number before it is compared with this, as claude-hud rounds it, so a reading within half a point below counts as at it. It is the context bar's own threshold, apart from bands.criticalAt, which colours the other bars and the context row's cache hit share, and its default is claude-hud's contextCriticalThreshold, which also starts claude-hud's breakdown.

breakdownAt.description: The whole percentage of the context window from which the token breakdown appears, with context.breakdown set to critical; while it is unset the breakdown appears from context.criticalAt. The percentage is rounded to a whole number before it is compared with this, as claude-hud rounds it, so a reading within half a point below counts as at it. It need not relate to context.warnAt or context.criticalAt, since it decides when a piece of information is shown and not a colour, so it may sit below, at or above either. A layer may write null to return it to unset when a shallower layer sets it.

autoCompactWindow.description: A window in tokens to measure the context against instead of the model's, matching the figure /context gives once Claude Code compacts before the window is full. While it is set, the row draws nothing from a frame whose tokens held (total_input_tokens) are absent (missing, or not a finite number of 0 or more), since without them there is nothing to measure against it, and measures a frame reporting 0 as 0% (a frame reporting no use may first be given the session's last good frame, its tokens held included); while it is unset the model's own window is used. A layer may write null to return it to unset when a shallower layer sets it.

estimate.description: What to draw when the client reports no percentage of the window in use (a negative one counts as none), or reports 0 while tokens are already held (which is how a client says it has not worked it out yet): never (nothing is estimated: a percentage reported from 0 to 100 is drawn as it is, one above 100 as 100, and a negative or missing one draws nothing), raw (the tokens held over the window), or buffered (that, plus the 16.5% of the window Claude Code reserves for compaction, rising from nothing at 5% of the window held to the whole reserve at 50%). This applies to the frame the row draws: a frame reporting no use may first be given the session's last good frame or the percentage its newest compaction left.

breakdown.description: Whether to add the input and cache tokens of the last request to the context row: critical adds them once the percentage the row draws (for the frame it draws, which context.estimate describes: the one the frame reports, or the estimate context.estimate makes, or, with context.autoCompactWindow set, the tokens held over that window), rounded to a whole number, reaches the breakdown threshold, which is context.breakdownAt, or context.criticalAt while that is unset, and never leaves them off. With no percentage to draw the row draws nothing, and the breakdown is of the last request the frame the row draws reports, so a frame given the session's last good frame draws, for instance, that frame's, and there is none to add while the frame drawn reports no last request.

text.description: A line of your own text to draw, in colours.custom; empty draws nothing. It is refused when longer than 80 characters or when it holds control, format or separator characters, and words are separated by single spaces. A character that passes but draws nothing, such as a braille blank, is removed, and the line is cut to the usable width.

position.description: Where the custom line sits: first draws it above the header, and last below the last row, as a line of its own in either layout mode.

command.description: The program and arguments the extra segment runs, as a list and not a shell string (for example ["git", "describe", "--tags"]). The first line of its standard output that shows something, or the label of a JSON object it prints, is the segment; a line with nothing a person could see in it, such as spaces, zero-width characters or an escape sequence alone, is skipped. Escape sequences are removed from the whole output first, so an operating system command with no terminator removes everything up to the next escape character or the end of the output, line breaks included. A command that fails or prints nothing draws nothing. It is refused when it has more than 16 arguments (the program included), when an argument is longer than 1024 characters or holds a NUL, and when the program starts with a dash. It runs on every refresh with your privileges and the statusline's whole environment. Its output is written to a file the system limits in size. That limit applies to every file it writes and every process it starts, so a program that writes a large cache is stopped and draws nothing, and so does one whose output reaches the limit. A process it starts is left running when it is killed for outrunning its time limit or when a newer update cancels the refresh. Because it runs a program with your privileges, only your own configuration may set it. That means the global config, a profile in your config-profiles directory, a directory rule or a command-line assignment. A project file such as .agent-shim.json is refused, though it may select one of your profiles by name, and a config write through the door's API (an MCP agent or the web client with the writes grant) is refused the extra settings for the same reason.

warnAt.description: The whole percentage of use at which a bar other than the context bar turns yellow when bar.gradient is off (the context bar has context.warnAt); it must be below criticalAt. A bar.gradient of use holds the warning colour exactly there, and width colours a bar by its cells, not its use, once a cell of its used part is drawn; both fall back to the band colours when a stop's colour is default or dim, and width also when no cell of its used part is drawn. The context row's cache hit share is coloured by these bands too.

criticalAt.description: The whole percentage of use at which a bar other than the context bar turns red when bar.gradient is off (the context bar has context.criticalAt). A bar.gradient of use holds the critical colour from there, and width colours a bar by its cells, not its use, once a cell of its used part is drawn; both fall back to the band colours when a stop's colour is default or dim, and width also when no cell of its used part is drawn. The context row's cache hit share is coloured by these bands too.

fiveHour.description: The name of the five-hour window; empty uses the language's own name for it.

sevenDay.description: The name of the weekly window; empty uses the language's own name for it.

width.description: A bar's width in cells before the line's spare width is shared out among the bars.

gradient.description: How a bar's used part is coloured: off (the default) draws the band's single colour, the bar's own colour below the warning threshold, the warning colour from there and the critical one from the critical threshold; use blends the bar's colour with its use, from its own colour at none in use to the warning colour at the warning threshold and the critical one at the critical threshold, holding exactly the colour the bar draws without a gradient at each threshold (the context bar's sit half a point below its whole percentages) and the critical colour above it; and width colours each cell of the used part across the bar's width, from the bar's own colour at the first cell to the critical one at the last, whatever the use, with a bar one cell wide drawing that cell in its own colour. A bar's thresholds are bands.warnAt and bands.criticalAt, and the context bar's are context.warnAt and context.criticalAt, and the figures beside a bar keep the band's colours in every mode. The unused part keeps colours.empty in every mode, and when that is default or dim, which set no colour of their own, it draws in the colour the used part ends in: under off the band's colour, under use the blend for the bar's use (even where no cell of the used part is drawn), and under width the last drawn cell's colour (the band's colour where no cell is drawn). A gradient blends RGB values, so a colour name, or a palette index below 16, is blended at the default RGB the xterm scheme gives it rather than the shade a themed terminal draws it in, while a stop itself, where a mode holds it exactly, is drawn as the bands draw that role. A bar whose stops include a role set to default or dim, which names no colour of its own, is drawn in the band's single colour: for use those stops are the bar's own, warning and critical roles, and for width its own and critical roles. A width bar with no cell of its used part drawn has no cell to colour, so it takes the band's colours as off does.

filled.description: The character that draws the used part of a bar.

empty.description: The character that draws the unused part of a bar.

value.description: Whether a quota window's figure is the share of it used or the share left; the bar and the colour always follow the share used.

bar.description: Whether each quota window is drawn as a bar, or as text alone.

compact.description: Whether the quota windows are drawn as one short line of text (`5h: 25% (1h 30m)`) in place of bars; it takes precedence over usage.bar.

resetLabel.description: Whether a window's reset time is introduced with `resets in` (`resets` for a wall-clock time), as in `(resets in 1h 30m)`, rather than the bare `(1h 30m)`.

modelScoped.description: Whether the per-model weekly windows the client reports (rate_limits.model_scoped) are drawn after the five-hour and weekly windows (one reported with a null, missing or non-numeric figure is drawn as two hyphens beside its reset); they describe the signed-in account, so a session that selected a provider never shows them, nor does a Bedrock session, whose subscription windows do not apply.

timeFormat.description: How a window's reset is shown: the time left (`1h 30m`), the wall-clock time (`at 14:30`), both, the share of the window already gone (`53% elapsed`), or that share and the wall-clock time. A window whose length is not known shows no share.

threshold.description: The whole percentage of use that at least one quota window must reach for the quota row to be drawn at all, the use compared after rounding to a whole percentage, as claude-hud compares it; 0 never hides it. A Bedrock session that selected no provider draws no five-hour, weekly or per-model window, whatever this is.

sevenDayThreshold.description: The whole percentage of use at which the weekly window is drawn beside the five-hour one, the use compared after rounding to a whole percentage, as claude-hud compares it; below it the weekly window is hidden, and 0 never hides it. A weekly window with no five-hour window beside it is never hidden by this setting. A Bedrock session that selected no provider draws no five-hour, weekly or per-model window, so this setting has nothing to hide there, and usage.threshold can still hide the whole row.

hourCycle.description: The hour cycle of a wall-clock time: `auto` follows the system locale, `h23` and `h24` are 24-hour time (`h24` writes midnight as 24:00), and `h12` and `h11` are 12-hour time with am or pm (`h11` writes the hour after midnight as 0).

seconds.description: Whether a wall-clock time includes seconds (`14:30:07`).

routed.description: Whether the cost segments draw for a session routed through a provider or a cloud platform's model id, where the client's own figure is not what was billed; the figure drawn is then priced from the door's usage log with `agent-shim model price`, else the client's own when it is above zero.

threshold.description: The fewest configuration items in total (CLAUDE.md files, rules, MCP servers and hook events) that must exist for the environment row to draw its counts.

parts.description: The parts of the sessionTime row to draw, in drawing order: when the session started, and how long ago the last response was written; a part left out is hidden, and an empty list hides the row.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the prompt cache lives, in seconds, when the transcript has not yet shown which tier the session writes (five minutes or one hour); the tier the transcript shows takes over once it does.

nameMaxLength.description: The most terminal columns of a tool's name the tools row draws, cut with an ellipsis. With a limit set, a tool of an MCP server is shown by its own name, without the server's, whether or not it needs cutting. 0 draws every name whole, an MCP tool's with its server.

maxVisible.description: The most kinds of finished tool call the tools row names, the most-used first, with the rest counted as +N more. 0 names every kind.

context.description: The colour of the context bar below the warning threshold while bar.gradient is off, of the figures beside it below that threshold in every mode, of a cache hit share above 100 less bands.warnAt percent, and the colour a bar.gradient of use or width blends the context bar from (at none in use for use, at the first cell for width), while a gradient bar with a stop whose colour is default or dim, or a width bar with no cell of its used part drawn, takes the band's colours.

usage.description: The colour of the quota bars and the memory bar below the warning threshold while bar.gradient is off, of the figures beside them below that threshold in every mode, and the colour a bar.gradient of use or width blends those bars from (at none in use for use, at the first cell for width), while a gradient bar with a stop whose colour is default or dim, or a width bar with no cell of its used part drawn, takes the band's colours.

warning.description: The colour of the context bar from context.warnAt up to context.criticalAt when bar.gradient is off (a bar.gradient of use holds it exactly where the bar turns yellow, and a gradient bar with a stop whose colour is default or dim draws the band's colours instead, and so does a width bar with no cell of its used part drawn), of the figures beside the bar from that threshold up to context.criticalAt in every mode, and of a cache hit share above 100 less bands.criticalAt percent and at most 100 less bands.warnAt percent.

usageWarning.description: The colour of a quota bar or the memory bar from bands.warnAt up to bands.criticalAt when bar.gradient is off (a bar.gradient of use holds it exactly at bands.warnAt, and a gradient bar with a stop whose colour is default or dim draws the band's colours instead, and so does a width bar with no cell of its used part drawn), and of the figures beside the bar from that threshold up to bands.criticalAt in every mode.

critical.description: The colour of a bar at or above its critical threshold (context.criticalAt for the context bar, bands.criticalAt for any other bar) when bar.gradient is off or use, of the last cell of a full bar more than one cell wide under a bar.gradient of width (a bar one cell wide draws its cell in its own colour, and a width bar whose own colour or this one is default or dim, or that has no cell of its used part drawn, draws the band's colours instead), of the figures beside a bar from its critical threshold in every mode, and of a cache hit share of at most 100 less bands.criticalAt percent.

model.description: The colour of the model and provider segments.

label.description: The colour of labels and secondary text: row labels, and the route, account, identity and headroom segments.

empty.description: The colour of the unused part of a bar.

project.description: The colour of the project path segment.

git.description: The colour of the version control segment's wrapper text (`git:(` and `)`).

gitBranch.description: The colour of the branch or bookmark and its ahead, behind and dirty markers.

activity.description: The colour of the names of the tools, skills and MCP servers the tools, skills and mcp rows draw. Their running markers take colours.warning and their finished markers colours.context.

agent.description: The colour of an agent's type in the agents row.

custom.description: The colour of the custom line.

pathLevels.description: How many trailing directories of the working directory the project segment shows: 1, 2 or 3, or full for the whole absolute path.

addedDirsLayout.description: Where the directories added to the session are drawn: inline, as +name after the project path in the project segment, or row, as an Added dirs line when layout.rows lists addedDirs.

enabled.description: Whether the vcs segment and the gitFiles row read the working directory's git status.

showDirty.description: Whether the branch is followed by * when the working tree has uncommitted changes.

showAheadBehind.description: Whether the branch is followed by the commits ahead of (up-arrow) and behind (down-arrow) its upstream.

showLineDiff.description: Whether the segment shows the total lines added and removed against HEAD, as [+a -d].

branchOverflow.description: How the vcs segment sits beside the project segment when they are listed next to each other: truncate keeps them as one unit the client cuts off at the terminal's edge, and wrap lets the line break between them.

pushWarnAt.description: The count of unpushed commits at which the ahead marker takes colours.warning; 0 turns it off.

pushCriticalAt.description: The count of unpushed commits at which the ahead marker takes colours.critical; 0 turns it off.

enabled.description: Whether the vcs segment reads a Jujutsu repository's status, instead of git's, when the working directory is inside one.

showDirty.description: Whether the bookmark or change id is followed by * when the working-copy commit differs from its parent.

showConflicts.description: Whether the segment shows !conflict when the working-copy commit has an unresolved conflict.
